concept.name: Rejection
concept.definition: In auction market theory, rejection is the market demonstrating disagreement with a price zone by refusing to spend time there: price probes a level, finds no two-sided trade, and moves away quickly, leaving thin TPO rows, single prints, or a tail. Rejection of prices beyond value is the structural basis of tails, excess, and failed breakouts.
concept.intuition: Rejection is the market taking one look at a price and leaving — the auction tried the level and found no takers.
concept.mechanics: Read from rapid passage (single-print rows), tails at extremes, or immediate re-entry into the prior value area after a probe beyond it; practitioners pair rejection structure with footprint evidence such as absorption at the tested level.
concept.failure_modes: What looks like rejection can be mere hesitation before acceptance; labeling a probe as rejection in real time is a judgment call that fails often enough to demand confirmation.
concept.misconceptions: Rejection wicks and tails do not guarantee reversal — a rejected level can be retested and accepted later the same day, at which point the earlier rejection loses its meaning.
concept.example: Price pokes 8 points above the prior VAH, prints only single TPOs there, and closes back inside value; the probe is recorded as rejection, and the prior value area remains the operative reference.

citations.source: GoCharting — Market Profile Trading: The Complete Guide (time skipped over a price is rejection)
WindoTrader — Market Profile Glossary (rejection at openings; tails)
